newsitem.title: ESTONIA: EU CAUTIONS ESTONIA OVER TRADE DEFICIT.
newsitem.headline: EU CAUTIONS ESTONIA OVER TRADE DEFICIT.

text.p: European commissioner Hans van den Broek on Tuesday cautioned Estonia to keep a watch on its rising trade deficit.
"Such a trade deficit, even if covered at present by capital inflows, is not sustainable in the long run," van den Broek told a news conference during a two-day visit to Estonia.
Estonia's current account deficit increased to 5.3 billion kroons in 1996 compared to 1995's 0.9 billion kroons.
The trade deficit in February was 1.1 billion kroons versus 1.2 billion kroons in January.
"There is a need to strengthen your competitive position on European and world markets," he added.
He said the cautionary note was aimed at encouraging Estonia to attract more foreign investments.
"We see it as an encouragement to continue the policy of attracting foreign investment and creating the economic conditions for more foreign direct foreign investment," he said.
"This will help boost exports and bring the trade more or less to balance," he added.
Some economic commentators see the rising trade imbalance as a reason to carry out a competitive devaluation of the kroon against the mark from its current eight kroons to one mark peg.
